headline: Gradient’s assumptions imply a 26% equity mix earns the most per unit of risk
takeaway: Why: Gradient assumes bonds earn slightly more per unit of risk on their own (0.37) than developed or emerging equity (0.36 and 0.35), and that they barely move with equities (−0.03). Mixing the two cuts risk faster than return up to about 26% equity; past that, equity volatility dominates. Return targets, not this ratio, set most equity weights.
